text:
tara: heads up — started seeing OOM surge on prod after the kernel-priority rollout (last night). ~1200 500s in the last hour, mostly on AWQ models with fp8 path. attaching quick prof output below
kevin: ugh, saw alerts. initial glance suggests KV cache dtype mismatch + allocator pressure when batch sizes spike. profiler shows large transient peaks at kv_write time.
anika: can you paste profiler snippets? is this the new kernel selector that prefers the fp8-optimized GEMM?
tara: yes. profiler snippet:
```
[profiler] peak_gpu_mem: 24608MB
[profiler] alloc_stack: kernel_selector::choose(fp8_gemm) -> kv_cache::write -> allocator:slab_alloc
[perf] kv_write_latency_p90: 42ms (was 12ms)
[perf] batch_tail_mem_burst: +18%
```
ben: interesting — the fp8 GEMM reduces model weights but increases temporary workspace and forces KV to be written in fp8; when we upcast to fp16 for attention compute later we end up duplicating buffers in hot path. fragmentation worsens with many small requests.
kevin: repro on staging with stress tool: run `stresser --model awq-1.2 --qps 80 --burst 12` and you'll hit OOM within ~3 mins. I added a quick script to force kernel fallback and it stabilizes.
tara: what's the lowest-risk mitigation for prod right now? rollback kernel selector or introduce runtime KV upcast?
anika: short-term: rollout a targeted kernel-priority override for AWQ families to prefer the fp16-compatible kernels (less workspace variance). Medium-term: implement on-the-fly KV autoupcast for layers flagged as mixing precision.
ben: sketch of autoupcast rule: if model.quant=="awq" and layer.attn_dtype!=layer.kv_dtype -> at KV write time, upcast to fp16 for layers where subsequent compute will upcast. Pseudocode:
```
if model.quant == "awq" and layer.kv_dtype == "fp8" and layer.next_compute_dtype == "fp16":
    kv_buf = cast(kv_buf, "fp16", inplace=false)
    allocator.reserve_hint(kv_buf.size * 1.05)
```
This avoids duplicate in-place conversions and lets allocator place buffers in larger contiguous slab.
kevin: also add allocator holdback knob: keep a small reserve (eg 5-8% of GPU) for transient workspace during merges/compactions. We had something similar in beta: `--allocator-soft-reserve 0.07`
tara: can we deploy quick fix today? i can flip kernel-priority for the affected service to fallback mode while we ship autoupcast in a branch.
ci-bot: deploy queued: kernel-priority-override -> service/llm-hosted-42 (canary 10%).
sre-bot: alert suppression enabled for this incident for 30m to avoid noise.
anika: test notes for autoupcast PR: add unit tests for layer dtype detection, perf test for stresser showing memory peak delta, and a microbenchmark to ensure latency impact < 4% p99. Also add regression alert if kv_write_latency_p90 increases > 10ms.
ben: FYI — batch hinting might help too: add a per-route batch_hint cap to prevent burst of small requests packing into large memory spikes. Example config: `batch_hint: {max_batch: 8, tail_room: 32}`
tara: deployed kernel override; canary showing no OOMs in first 20m. will keep monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: next steps: 1) autoupcast RFC and PR, 2) allocator soft-reserve default enable for dedicated nodes, 3) add batch_hint guardrails to console presets.
anika: i'll own the RFC + tests. ben, can you prototype autoupcast branch?
ben: on it. starting with local repro then perf runs on p4d.
tara: closing loop: if we see reoccurrence after rollback, escalate to revert kernel-selector change. for now, holding until autoupcast validated. :eyes:
